findings.text: BIOS PUNIT family shares one base combined with offsets 0 to 27. Offsets cover zero placeholder, voltage regulator interface, PCS read and write, PCU config read and write, PL1 read and write, RAM voltage trigger, telemetry info and trace control and event control and trace data and event data read and write pairs, module temperature, one reserved slot, voltage override read and write, ratio override read and write, global voltage frequency control read and write, and SoC temperature threshold read and write.

GTD PUNIT family shares its own base combined with sparse offsets 0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 22, 23, 26 and 28. They cover zero placeholder, general config, ICCP license dynamic capacitance scale read and write, watermark query, config wish write, requested duty cycle read, voltage frequency change disable, and dynamic duty cycle control and tuning.

ISPD PUNIT family shares its own base combined with offsets 0 to 5. They cover zero placeholder, general config, ISP latency tolerance query, IU frequency bounds access, and dynamic capacitance level read and write.
PUNIT result codes are integers 0 to 6. Zero means success. Others distinguish invalid command, invalid parameter, command timeout, command locked, invalid regulator identifier, and regulator error.

Fallback IPC helper accepts a command word, two parameter words, and optional input and output word pointers, and reports absent device with a negative nodev result. It preserves linkage when no platform implementation exists.
Telemetry size caps are 28 static RAM events and 20 operating system allocated events. A header guard marks telemetry definitions included.

Telemetry model has units PSS first, IOSS second, and none terminator. Event log pairs 32 bit identifier with 64 bit value. Event config holds pointer to enabled identifiers plus event count below 29 and sampling period. Event map pairs name with identifier. Unit config holds event descriptors, iomem register base, used static RAM count, and current maximum and minimum periods. Platform config nests PSS and IOSS configs with power and IPC device links and in-use flag. Core operations offer per-unit verbosity get and set plus raw and cooked log readers taking unit, buffer, length, and all-events flag.

Platform telemetry config carries two mutexes, one for trace handling and one for general telemetry, guarding shared unit state and device links. In-use flag signals exclusive ownership. Verbosity and log operations require the matching mutex held.
Invalidate PCID types are 0 individual address, 1 single context, 2 all including globals, 3 all excluding globals.

Low level invalidate packages PCID and address as a 16 byte descriptor and issues the invalidate with a compiler memory barrier. Wrappers fix common cases: one address with PCID, one whole context with zero address, full flush including globals with zeros, and full flush excluding globals with zeros.

IO APIC register views overlay 32 bit raw word with packed fields. First exposes latch, delivery type, and identifier. Second exposes version, request and entry count. Third exposes arbitration priority. Fourth exposes boot target. Route entry is packed 64 bit with three overlays: normal delivery with vector, delivery mode, destination mode, status, polarity, remote, level, mask, reserved spans and destination identifiers; remapped form with shared, zero, index, format and reserved fields; and split low and high 32 bit words.
IO APIC mapping control uses value 1 to allocate and value 2 to check.
Port space spans 0 to 65535 inclusive. ISA IO base aliases the direct map base as an iomem pointer. Delay predicate reports true in this configuration so the slow path always delays.

Memory mapped IO generators produce typed readers and writers for byte, word, long and quad widths with barrier control. Ordered short names cover 8, 16, 32 and 64 bit access. Relaxed and raw aliases name the unordered forms. A 32 bit block copy moves a caller count with repeating string move and memory barrier. Memory copy helpers between IO and normal memory are architecture provided.

Port IO offers byte, word and long input, output and block string forms plus paused variants that transfer then invoke a slow-down delay. The slow path consults a predicate and otherwise calls the platform delay helper. Block transfers use per-element port loops when the guest string unroll attribute is present and repeating string port operations otherwise, with memory barriers.

Translation and mapping names are self-defined aliases showing architecture provision: virtual to physical and physical to virtual, ISA bus to virtual through physical to virtual, cached, uncached, write-combining, write-through, protected and encrypted remap forms, writeback remap, generic remap and unmap, device pointer translate pair, write-combining index add and reserve, RAM remap predicate, and valid range marker. Encrypted physical access predicate reports true for any address and size here.
IO bitmap state holds a 64 bit sequence, a reference count, a maximum byte count covering trailing zeros, and a fixed array of bitmap longs.

Invalidate helper writes an out-of-limit offset into the current CPU task state IO base so later user port access faults, staying correct even when virtualization rewrites the task limit. Public update and invalidate names alias native helpers. Share and exit helpers are empty in this configuration.
Sideband message offsets are D0 control, D4 data, and D8 extended control. Read mask, write mask, high byte mask, low byte mask, and enable value F0 control message formation.

Sideband opcodes distinguish memory, config, control-register, register and extended SRAM read and write pairs with values 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 16, 17, 18 and 19. Unit identifiers cover agent, system controller, CPU, bulk, power, graphics, system interrupt, clock, USB, SATA and PCIe blocks.

Software IO TLB enable is false. DMA remap timeout scales as ten thousand times the TSC kilohertz counter. Reserved memory sanity accepts a region only when firmware memory type is reserved or nonvolatile; otherwise it reports a firmware bug naming the inclusive range and returns invalid argument.

64 byte direct store moves one full line from source to destination with ordering constraints that keep other memory references outside it and with explicit addressing. An IO wrapper forwards an iomem destination to the same primitive. A submitter iterates a caller count of 64 byte lines from source to one iomem destination.

Enabled path reads an IO APIC register through the architecture APIC operations table. Legacy IRQ test treats numbers at or above legacy count or flagged in the APIC bitmap as APIC owned, and PCI assignment needs firmware entries plus enabled APIC IRQs. Disabled path uses constants: false IRQ and PCI tests, zero APICs, legacy top, identity GSI mapping, empty resource and suspend and setup actions, null native hooks, and memory errors for save and restore.

Reordering memory references around an invalidate that clears global entries can observe stale translations. The primitive needs a compiler barrier and callers should choose the narrowest type covering needed entries.
Using a remapping reserved region that firmware did not mark reserved or nonvolatile risks corrupting usable RAM. The sanity check must run before use and failure must abort mapping.
Repeating string port operations can be unsafe or badly emulated on some confidential guests. Block helpers must take the per-element path when the guest unroll attribute is present.
